grammar.explanation: 第一 modifies either verbs with に or nouns with or without の, and means "first." It is also used as a predicate with だ or です.
grammar.pattern_form: a. 第一にV：第一に考えられることは; 第一に挙げられる例は b. 第一のN：第一の問題; 第一の原因; 第一の注意すべき点 c. 第一N：第一条件(term); 第一印象(impression) d. Nが第一だ：安全が第一だ; 練習が第一だ

grammar.title: Nounに{関する／関して}
grammar.meaning_en: with regard to; regarding; concerning; about; on; related to
grammar.explanation: に関する literally means "related to," but it is also used to mean "with regard to; concerning." に関する modifies nouns and に関して modifies verbs. について is similar in meaning to に関して, but is less formal and is used in both written and spoken language.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N1に関するN2：日本の教育に関する問題 b. Nに関してV：家康の政治(politics)に関してディスカッションをする c. Nに関してはS：読み方に関しては色々あると言われている

grammar.title: 考えられない
grammar.meaning_en: unimaginable; unthinkable; inconceivable
grammar.explanation: 考えられない (lit. cannot think) is preceded by either nouns or sentences.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N{は／なんて}考えられない b. S-plain{ということは／なんて}考えられない

grammar.title: 生かす
grammar.meaning_en: make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain
grammar.explanation: 生かす literally means "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, skills, experience, etc.," "to utilize to the fullest a special property of something," or "to take advantage of an opportunity."

grammar.title: Sentenceことから
grammar.meaning_en: because; from the fact that ~
grammar.explanation: Sことから is used to express a reason.
grammar.pattern_form: Type 2c

grammar.title: Nounなし
grammar.meaning_en: without ~; with no ~
grammar.explanation: Xなし means "without X" and is used with で to modify verbs, with の to modify nouns, and with だ to form a predicate.
grammar.pattern_form: Nなし{で／の／だ}

grammar.title: こそ
grammar.meaning_en: the very ~; It is that ~; in particular; precisely; definitely; for sure; only (when, by doing ~, etc.)
grammar.explanation: こそ emphasizes the preceding word, phrase or clause. When こそ is used, the particles は, が and を are usually dropped.
grammar.pattern_form: a. Nこそ：今度こそ; これこそ b. V-teこそ：(日本語で)話してこそ

grammar.title: Verb-masu込む
grammar.meaning_en: in; into; deeply; heavily; thoroughly; completely
grammar.explanation: The compound verb base 込む can mean the following: a. Taking or putting something/someone into something (Exs. 飲み込む; 取り込む; つめ込む; 押し込む) b. Getting into something (Exs. 入り込む; 乗り込む; 飛び込む; あがり込む) c. Being heavily involved in something (Exs. 考え込む; 話し込む; 寝込む) d. Doing something thoroughly or completely (Exs. 教え込む; 思い込む; 信じ込む)
grammar.pattern_form: Verb-masu込む

grammar.title: ～さ(あ)
grammar.meaning_en: (you know)
grammar.explanation: さ occurs after phrases, clauses or sentences in very casual conversation. One function is to catch the hearer's attention, but it is also used as a filler with no meaning.
grammar.pattern_form: phrase/clause/sentenceさ

grammar.title: Nounでもある
grammar.meaning_en: be also
grammar.explanation: XはYでもある is used to introduce the second property of X when X has more than one property. Note that XもYだ is used when someone/something else is also Y. Compare the following sentences: 田中さんは先生だ。田中さんは画家でもある。 山田さんは先生だ。田中さんも先生だ。
grammar.pattern_form: N/ANaでもある

grammar.title: ずっと
grammar.meaning_en: all the time; all along; all the way; all through ~; throughout ~; ever (since); never (since)
grammar.explanation: ずっと means that a state or action is ongoing, from one point in time to another point in time (often the moment of speech).

grammar.title: Number1, Number2 + Counter
grammar.meaning_en: (two or three) days/times/etc.; (three, four) hours/cars/etc.
grammar.explanation: Two successive numbers are used to indicate an approximate number or amount.
grammar.pattern_form: Number1, Number2 + Counter【Number2 is the subsequent number.】： 2、3回; 3、4時間; 3、4日; 5、6枚; 5、6本

grammar.title: ～まま
grammar.meaning_en: Xままだ = remain the same as ~ Xまま(で)V = V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~ Xままにする = leave ~ as (it is)
grammar.explanation: まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
grammar.pattern_form: a. Nのまま：Tシャツのまま; 子供のまま b. DemAまま：このまま; そのまま; あのまま c. Aまま：冷たいまま d. ANaなまま：きれいなまま e. V-plain.pastまま：置いたまま; 作ったまま

grammar.title: ～代
grammar.meaning_en: 10/20/30/etc. + 代 = one's teens/twenties/thirties/etc. 1900/1910/1920/etc. + 年代 = 1900s/1910s/1920s/etc.
grammar.explanation: The suffix 代 is used with ten or its multiples to describe someone's approximate age, or with ten or its multiples and 年 to refer to a certain decade.

grammar.title: ～(の)姿
grammar.meaning_en: N姿 = in ~; wearing ~ Nの姿 = one's appearance; in ~; wearing ~ V-plain.non-past姿 = the way one V
grammar.explanation: 姿 means "appearance; figure." It is used to describe someone's external appearance, i.e., someone's form or physical appearance; someone's appearance in certain clothing; or the way someone appears when he/she is doing something.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N(の)姿：着物姿; 女性の姿 b. V-plain.non-past姿：歩く姿; 話している姿

grammar.title: Verbては、Verb
grammar.meaning_en: V1 and V2 repeatedly/over and over again/many times/etc.
grammar.explanation: The construction V-teはV is used when a set of actions is repeated over a period of time. V-teはV can be repeated, as seen in Ex. 3.
grammar.pattern_form: V1-teは、V2

grammar.title: Verbたものだ
grammar.meaning_en: used to ~; would
grammar.explanation: V-plain.pastものだ is used to describe in a nostalgic fashion what someone did or what happened in the past.
grammar.pattern_form: V-plain.pastものだ

grammar.title: だんだん
grammar.meaning_en: gradually; little by little; bit by bit
grammar.explanation: だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ～ていく, てくる and ～くなる, ～になる, ～ようになる.

grammar.title: ～につれて
grammar.meaning_en: as ~; with ~
grammar.explanation: Xにつれて indicates that something takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-verb (i.e., VN).
grammar.pattern_form: a. V-non-past.affにつれて：文法が分かるにつれて b. Nにつれて：経済の発展につれて

grammar.title: Verb-masu上げる
grammar.meaning_en: up; finish up V-ing
grammar.explanation: Affixed to the masu-stems of verbs, 上げる forms compound verbs, adding meanings such as "finish something up," "upward," or "to a great extent." The meaning is determined by the preceding verb.
grammar.pattern_form: V-masu上げる：書き上げる; し上げる; 縛り上げる(to tie up); 磨き上げる(to polish); 読み上げる(to read aloud); 持ち上げる; 立ち上げる(to start/boot up)

grammar.title: Verb-masuがけに
grammar.meaning_en: on one's way
grammar.explanation: がけに with the masu-stems of motion verbs like 行く, 来る, and 帰る means "on one's way."
grammar.pattern_form: V-masuがけに(V=motion verbs)：行きがけに; 来がけに; 帰りがけに

grammar.title: ～だけで
grammar.meaning_en: just with ~; just by V-ing (is fine/enough/etc.); just N (is fine/enough/etc.)
grammar.explanation: N/Vだけで is used to express the idea that just X or just doing X is fine or good enough or that one can do something just with X or by doing X.
grammar.pattern_form: a. Nだけで：日本語だけで; 漢字の勉強だけで b. V1-plainだけでV2：(インターネットで)注文{する／した}だけで c. {V-plain.non-past/N}だけで{いい／十分(enough)だ／etc.}：ビデオを見るだけでいい; 英和辞典だけで十分だ

grammar.title: あまりに(も)
grammar.meaning_en: too; excessively; so
grammar.explanation: あまりに(も) indicates that the degree of something is excessively high. It is commonly used in formal language.
grammar.pattern_form: a. あまりに(も){A/ANaだ}：あまりに(も)古い; あまりに(も)不自然だ b. あまりに(も){Adv/ANaに/A-stemく}：あまりに(も)ゆっくり; あまりに(も)簡単に; あまりに(も)速く

grammar.title: ～には
grammar.meaning_en: to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when
grammar.explanation: には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (= ～時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Compare the following examples: 漢字を覚えるにはフラッシュカード{が効果的だ[judgement]／×を使っている[action]} 漢字を覚えるためにフラッシュカード{を使っている／×が効果的だ} ためには can be used to indicate judgement, as shown below: 漢字を覚える{には／ためには}フラッシュカードが効果的だ。
grammar.pattern_form: a. V-plain.non-past.affには：見るには; 話すには b. Nには(N:the stems of suru-verbs (i.e., VN) or the direct object of する)：旅行には; 仕事には

grammar.title: だいたい
grammar.meaning_en: だいたいV = mostly V; nearly V; almost V だいたいのN = most N; almost all N; approximate N; rough N だいたいNumber/Amount = approximately Number/Amount
grammar.explanation: だいたい means "most; almost; nearly (all); approximate." The meaning changes depending on what だいたい modifies, as seen in 英訳.
grammar.pattern_form: a. だいたいV b. だいたいのN c. だいたいNumber/Amount

grammar.title: Nounに{おける／おいて}
grammar.meaning_en: in; at; on; during
grammar.explanation: The compound particle における indicates the place or time of an action, event or state. The pre-verbal form is において. Both are used only in formal language.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N1におけるN2：日本における生活 b. NにおいてV：日本において生活する

grammar.title: ～もまた
grammar.meaning_en: as well; also; too
grammar.explanation: In this usage もまた means the same as も; however, it is more emphatic and formal than も. また has several meanings, but in this use また is synonymous with も.

grammar.title: なんだ
grammar.meaning_en: Oh!
grammar.explanation: The literal meaning of なんだ is "What is X?" However, it can also be used as an interjection to express the speaker's slight surprise.

grammar.title: ほら
grammar.meaning_en: Look!; See?; Come on!
grammar.explanation: The interjection ほら is used to draw the hearer's attention to something.

grammar.title: ～を除いて
grammar.meaning_en: except (for) ~; with the exception of ~; but ~
grammar.explanation: 除く means "to remove; get rid of." を除いて is used as a compound particle meaning "except."
grammar.pattern_form: a. Nを除いて b. N1を除くN2

grammar.title: すなわち
grammar.meaning_en: that is; i.e.; namely
grammar.explanation: すなわち is used to rephrase something that has just been mentioned.
grammar.pattern_form: NP1/S1、すなわちNP2/S2：日本で一番大きい町、すなわち東京

grammar.title: 一応
grammar.meaning_en: for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case
grammar.explanation: 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.

grammar.title: 左右する
grammar.meaning_en: influence; govern
grammar.explanation: 左右する means "to influence" or "to govern." It is commonly used in written language.
grammar.pattern_form: N1はN2を左右する

grammar.title: Noun1、Noun2共(に)
grammar.meaning_en: Both X and Y
grammar.explanation: N1、N2共(に) means "both N1 and N2." The colloquial form is N1もN2も.
grammar.pattern_form: N1、N2共に：九州、四国共に; 男女とも(に)

grammar.title: (期間の表現)に入る
grammar.meaning_en: N(time period)に入る = N sets in; N begins N(time period)に{入り／入って(から)} = since N began; after N began
grammar.explanation: Nに入る literally means "enter N," but when N is a noun indicating a time period, the phrase means "N begins." The most common form is Nに入り or Nに入って(から), meaning "since/after N began."
grammar.pattern_form: N(time period)に{入る／入り／入って(から)}

grammar.title: ～を問題にする; ～が問題にされる; ～が問題になる
grammar.meaning_en: Xを問題にする = to bring X up as an issue; to address the issue/question of X; to question X; to call X into question Xが問題に{される／なる} = X becomes an issue; X is brought up as an issue; X is questioned; X is called into question
grammar.explanation: Xを問題にする means "to bring X up as an issue" or "to question X." This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N/NPを問題にする b. N/NPが問題に{される／なる}

grammar.title: 未だに
grammar.meaning_en: still; (not ~) yet
grammar.explanation: 未だに indicates that someone or something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. 未だ(に) is used primarily in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.

grammar.title: いかに～か
grammar.meaning_en: how; how much; in what way
grammar.explanation: This structure occurs as an embedded interrogative sentence, where いかに means "how (much)" or "in what way." いかに is commonly used in written language.
grammar.pattern_form: Type 3

grammar.title: しかしながら
grammar.meaning_en: however; but
grammar.explanation: しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is usually used in written language.
grammar.pattern_form: S1。しかしながら、S2。

grammar.title: かなり
grammar.meaning_en: considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot
grammar.explanation: かなり indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high but is higher than average.

grammar.title: Verb{れる／られる}
grammar.explanation: Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masuになる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and 召し上がる. Note that the polite form of the auxiliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる (see 文型 d). The auxiliary verb おられる is less polite that いらっしゃる.
grammar.pattern_form: a. う-verbs：V-nai + れる：書かれる; 話される; 使われる; 飲まれる b. る-verbs：V-masu + られる：起きられる; 寝られる c. Irr.verbs：される; 来られる d. V-teいる：V-teおられる：住んでおられる; 持っておられる; 知っておられる

grammar.title: Noun次第
grammar.meaning_en: N次第だ = depend on ~ N次第で = depending on ~
grammar.explanation: When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
grammar.pattern_form: N次第{だ／で}：成績次第{だ／で}; 大学次第{だ／で}

grammar.title: ～とは限らない
grammar.meaning_en: not necessarily ~; not always; it's not necessarily the case that ~
grammar.explanation: Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional as shown in 文型.
grammar.pattern_form: Type 1/Type 3 (Both forms are acceptable.)

grammar.title: ちゃんと; きちんと
grammar.meaning_en: neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail
grammar.explanation: ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly or without fail (i.e., in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと.

grammar.title: 少なくとも～は
grammar.meaning_en: at (the) least; to say the least
grammar.explanation: 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or a number (optionally followed by a counter). When 少なくとも is used with a noun, は often follows the noun (or the particle after the noun), indicating that the noun is under focus. When は follows a number (+ a counter), it emphasizes the number.
grammar.pattern_form: a. 少なくともNumber(+Counter)：少なくとも20ぐらいの国; 少なくとも3時間は b. 少なくともN：少なくとも家族(は)

grammar.title: ～もVerbば、～もVerb
grammar.meaning_en: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well
grammar.explanation: This structure is used to present actions or states (usually two) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
grammar.pattern_form: a. N1もV-condば、N2もV (See L.6 文法ノート③) b. A-stemくもV-condば、～も：面白くもなれば、つまらなくもなる c. ANa{に／で}もV-condば、～も：上手にもなれば、下手にもなる; 安全でもあれば、便利でもある d. V1-masuもすれば、V2-masuもする：読みもすれば、書きもする

grammar.title: ～のうち(で)
grammar.meaning_en: in; of; among
grammar.explanation: Xのうち(で) is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
grammar.pattern_form: Nのうち(で)

grammar.title: 後(の)Noun
grammar.meaning_en: the remaining ~; the remainder of ~; the rest of ~
grammar.explanation: 後の, when followed by a number (+ counter) or a noun, means "the remaining" or "the rest of." Here, の after 後 is optional. This use of 後 should be distinguised from 後 in the following example, where 後 means "~more." In this use, の cannot occur after 後. このプロジェクトには{後三人／×後の三人}必要だ。(We need three more people for this project.)
grammar.pattern_form: a. 後(の)Number(+Counter)：後(の)一人; 後(の)3台 b. 後のN：後の人たち; 後の車

grammar.title: 何より(も)
grammar.meaning_en: before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~
grammar.explanation: 何より(も) means "before everything" or "than anything else," depending on the context.

grammar.title: ～に従って
grammar.meaning_en: in accordance with ~; complying with ~; following ~
grammar.explanation: に従って literally means "following." In some contexts, it means "in accordance with."
grammar.pattern_form: Nに従って：スケジュールに従って; 規則に従って

grammar.title: たった(の)Number(+Counter)
grammar.meaning_en: only
grammar.explanation: たった(の) is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
grammar.pattern_form: たった(の)Number(+Counter)：たった(の)三人; たった(の)15

grammar.title: ～て{しかたがない／しようがない／しょうがない}
grammar.meaning_en: cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~
grammar.explanation: てしかたがない, てしようがない, etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しかたがない and しようがない are interchangeable. しょうがない is colloquial. This use is different from the following example, where しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。来年まで待とう。
grammar.pattern_form: a. {V/A}-teしかたがない, etc.：咳が出てしかたがない; 喉が渇いてしかたがない; 寒くてしようがない; 欲しくてしょうがない b. ANaでしかたがない, etc.：心配でしかたがない; 退屈(boring)でしかたがない

grammar.title: ～以来
grammar.meaning_en: since
grammar.explanation: 以来 means "since." It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
grammar.pattern_form: a. V-te以来：21世紀に入って以来 b. VN/N以来：終戦以来; 結婚以来; 入学以来; 留学以来 c. それ／あれ以来

grammar.title: 何から何まで
grammar.meaning_en: anything and everything; all; all kinds
grammar.explanation: 何から何まで means "all." It is more emphatic than 全部, すべて or みんな. 何から何まで can be used with 全部, すべて or みんな.

grammar.title: かえって
grammar.meaning_en: on the contrary; rather
grammar.explanation: かえって is used when an opposite result comes about, contrary to one's expectation.

grammar.title: ～と同時に
grammar.meaning_en: as soon as; the moment; at the same time; also; as well
grammar.explanation: と同時に means that something takes place at the same time as other actions or events, or that something is the case while something else is also the case.
grammar.pattern_form: a. {V/A}-plain.non-pastと同時に：{考える／考えない／考えている}と同時に; 難しいと同時に b. {ANa/N}{である／じゃない／ではない}と同時に：大切{である／じゃない／ではない}と同時に; 問題{である／じゃない／ではない}と同時に c. VN/Nと同時に：終戦と同時に; 叫び声と同時に

grammar.title: Sentenceっけ
grammar.explanation: っけ is a question marker. It is used only in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of verbs, adjectives and ～ない, んだ must be used before っけ, as seen in 文型.
grammar.pattern_form: a. {V/A}-plain.non-pastんだっけ：行くんだっけ; 大きいんだっけ b. {V/A}-plain.past(んだ)っけ：行った(んだ)っけ; 大きかった(んだ)っけ c. {ANa/N/QW}(なん)だっけ：上手(なん)だっけ; 学生(なん)だっけ; いつ(なん)だっけ d. {ANa/N}じゃないんだっけ：上手じゃないんだっけ; 学生じゃないんだっけ e. {ANa/N/QW}だった(んだ)っけ：上手だった(んだ)っけ; 学生だった(んだ)っけ; いつだった(んだ)っけ f. {ANa/N}じゃなかった(んだ)っけ：上手じゃなかった(んだ)っけ; 学生じゃなかった(んだ)っけ
